title.narrative: Reforming the Police Service for Socio-Economic Transformation in Kenya

description.narrative: Kenya has undertaken various police reform efforts over the past two decades, focusing on institutional, legal, policy, operational, and administrative dimensions critical to transforming the police service. The overarching goal has been to build an efficient, professional, accountable, and trusted police service that ensures public safety and security. While progress has been made, reforms have been uneven, with setbacks such as the 2007–2008 post-election violence highlighting persistent structural and operational challenges. The 2010 Constitution provided renewed momentum for change, yet significant work remains to fully align policing with constitutional values and public expectations.This programmatic intervention seeks to accelerate police reform as a foundation for rule of law, human rights, safety, and sustainable development. It prioritizes four strategic areas:Strengthening policy, institutional, and legislative frameworksEnhancing stakeholder coordination, public participation, and community engagementAdvancing strategic communications and knowledge managementBuilding institutional and human capacities for sustained police transformationThrough these focus areas, the intervention aims to support the development of a modern, accountable, and people-centered policing system in Kenya.
